script.user: Cap the upload client's retry backoff. A flaky connection waits minutes between tries. Keep its public API as it is.

script.say: The delay doubles from 500 ms with no ceiling, so any raise of MAX_TRIES makes the waits grow without bound.

align.title: Cap the upload backoff
align.summary: Bound the wait between upload retries without changing the client's API.
findings: backoff() doubles the delay from 500 ms and has no ceiling.
finalize() goes through send(), so it is retried like any part.
approach: Add delayFor(n) with a ceiling, and use it in backoff().
Pin the delays with a unit test.

rejected.why: Fewer tries fail more uploads on a flaky connection; the waits are the problem.

questions.ask: How long may one wait between tries be?

options.label: 30 s
options.tradeoff: Rides out a short outage; at most about a minute over 5 tries.

options.label: 10 s
options.tradeoff: Snappier, but gives up during a longer drop.

recommendation.why: Long enough for a network handover, short enough not to strand the user.

server-check.name: Is a retried finalize safe?
server-check.task: Read src/upload/client.ts. Can a retried finalize() commit an upload twice? Answer in 2 sentences with the evidence.

script.say: No: finalize() sends PUT /uploads/<id>/finalize, and a PUT on the same upload id is idempotent on the server. A retry after a lost response finalizes the same upload again, which is a no-op.
